The calibration crisis reveals a fundamental misalignment between model reliability and discriminative capacity. When RES≈0, maps become inactive, implying that calibration efforts fail to enhance discrimination. This suggests that the core issue lies not in scoring accuracy but in the signal-stack quality—specifically QB behavior and scheme dynamics. The structural deficit arises because post-hoc calibration cannot reduce ε_rank without improving the underlying signal. Thus, the fix is not in recalibrating scores but in refining the input signal layers. The dual failure mode involves both underperforming maps (due to low resolution) and poor discrimination (due to weak signal fidelity). These insights inform GSI’s Bayesian inference pipeline and GSE’s situational reasoning engine, which must prioritize signal integrity over calibration polish.
